why: A part on its own hyperthread pairs with more work than its vCPUs do runs its work at the sibling speed and waits for a vCPU past them, which its CPU share past 1 counts; the frozen engine 0.16.0 also counted the vCPUs taking turns at its own work, so its overloaded part ran at a hundredth of its speed, and saturated where its vCPUs fill at the speed of the peak (engine 1.6.0, ADR-0091). In the one recorded case with such a part, 4 vCPU at a sibling speed of 0.6 doing 10 ms of CPU a request at 300 req/s, these figures are the Java's own: its CPU, slot and overall shares, its load, its own time and the slots it holds for it, the busiest part's utilization, and the saturation point, 240 req/s, with the summary that names it, where its vCPUs fill at 0.6 of a core each. Each reads as the frozen engine's only where the Java's figure is the one listed (OwnFigures), and every other figure of the case is the frozen engine's (InstantEstimatorTests).

withHyperthreads_slowsThePartOnItsOwnThr./summary: Overloaded at 300 req/s: api needs 125% of its capacity; it saturates at about 240 req/s.
